title: Leaf symptom claims used by the leaf_spot pattern
source: AUTHORED, NOT QUOTED. Every claim below was written by Claude from model knowledge while building the leaf_spot pattern and leaf_differential on 2026-09-05. NONE of it was retrieved from, or checked against, a cited publication. It is recorded here so it stops masquerading as authority inside a diagnostic pattern, which is where it currently sits with no source field at all. The principal identified Utah State University Extension hemp materials as reaching the same conclusions independently; that document has NOT been retrieved or opened here, so it corroborates nothing yet - a citation nobody has read is not evidence.
authority_class_basis: Cannot be set. The work has not been read, and a class filled from a remembered impression is exactly the guessed standing field CLAUDE.md forbids. It becomes `treatise` or `extension_guidance` when a real document is ingested.
how_to_verify: Supply the USU Extension hemp publication as a PDF and run tools/ingest_pdf.py. That replaces this file with a citable work, and the claims below become quotable rather than asserted.

integrity.basis: Authored rather than quoted. Nothing vouches for this against a source because no source was opened.

sections.text: Calcium is immobile in the plant: it cannot be withdrawn from older tissue to supply new growth, so a calcium problem marks NEW tissue and never reverses in leaves already damaged.  [UNVERIFIED: authored from model knowledge, not retrieved from any publication. Used by leaf_differential - separates calcium from magnesium and potassium.]

integrity.basis: Authored rather than quoted. Nothing vouches for this against a source because no source was opened.

sections.text: Calcium moves with water. Adequate calcium in solution can still fail to reach new tissue if water transport is disrupted - a reservoir that ran low, a stopped feed, or impaired roots - so the meter can read correctly while the plant is calcium-starved.  [NOTE] This distinction came from the principal, not from this agent's original pattern, which collapsed both calcium failures into one.  [UNVERIFIED: authored from model knowledge, not retrieved from any publication. Used by leaf_differential - the calcium_transport_limitation hypothesis, which led on this plant and would have been missed entirely without it.]

integrity.basis: Authored rather than quoted. Nothing vouches for this against a source because no source was opened.

sections.text: Magnesium and potassium are mobile and are withdrawn from older leaves first, so their deficiencies mark OLD tissue. Both can produce rust-brown spotting or blotching.  [UNVERIFIED: authored from model knowledge, not retrieved from any publication. Used by leaf_differential - weakens both when new growth is affected.]

integrity.basis: Authored rather than quoted. Nothing vouches for this against a source because no source was opened.

sections.text: Septoria-type leaf spot usually presents as a brown lesion with a yellow halo. A halo therefore SCREENS FOR a pathogen and does not establish one: leaf spots also arise from abiotic causes, and a nutrient lesion can develop a chlorotic margin. Spread over days is the stronger discriminator; absence of a halo is the more useful half of the test.  [NOTE] An earlier version of the pattern stated 'a halo says pathogen' as a rule. The principal corrected it to a screening feature. That correction is the reason this file exists.  [UNVERIFIED: authored from model knowledge, not retrieved from any publication. Used by leaf_differential - the pathogen hypothesis.]

integrity.basis: Authored rather than quoted. Nothing vouches for this against a source because no source was opened.

sections.text: Many cannabis and hemp leaf problems are abiotic - nutrient deficiency, over- or under-watering, environmental stress - rather than pest or pathogen. A symptom-first classifier that reaches for pests is reaching for the less likely branch.  [UNVERIFIED: authored from model knowledge, not retrieved from any publication. Used by leaf_differential - ordering of the candidate list.]
